name: Muilearach

attributes.attribute: a sea goddess and a form of the Cailleach
a bald, one-eyed hag with a gray-blue face and sharp teeth
mother of the king of Lochlann, with a balm that healed
slain by the Fianna and under another name by Fionn

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Muilearach is a Scottish and Irish goddess of the sea. She is one form of the great goddess the tales call the Cailleach. As a hag of the sea she was a formidable figure, a bald, one-eyed being with a gray-blue face and teeth that stuck out sharp. She was known through the Scottish Highlands and on the isles of Lewis, Harris, and the southern Hebrides. She is an ancestral goddess and the mother of the king of the land of Lochlann. Her home was under the water. She had a gift of healing, for the pot of balm she carried made the sick well and the weak strong. The tales still feared her. The hero band the Fiann slew her in a great battle. Under the name Muireartach she is an Irish hag the tales know as the eastern sea. She lived beneath the ocean with a magic smith. She loved merchants who cut her waves, but she loved their goods more and might turn their boats to take it. The hero Fionn mac Cumhaill killed her after one more wreck was laid at her door.
